captions: Four robots share one delivery.
The mailbag must travel from the shelf, through the hatch, and onto the train.
There’s a second job.
Sign the delivery slip.
Which robot can do each job?
The orchestrator reads the depot’s knowledge graph in Relate.
Meet Jack, the forklift, and Patch, the mechanic.
Jack’s chassis supports lifting.
With a working fork carriage mounted, he can lift the tray.
To sign the delivery slip, a robot scans it.
Jack and Patch both have that skill.
Only Jack can lift the tray.
For the signature, the model can choose either robot.
It proposes a plan.
The validator checks who can do each job,
and what has to happen first.
The approved plan goes into Relate.
Watch the mailbag change hands.
The executor updates the graph.
That link now points to the courier.
Then Jack’s fork carriage slips.
The executor marks it offline.
Loading needs those forks,
and departure depends on loading.
Signing can still go ahead.
The orchestrator reads the changed graph.
Patch has a driver that fits the broken collar.
The model adds a repair before loading
and keeps the signature.
Jack signs with his scanner.
Patch tightens the collar.
Once the graph records the repair,
Jack can load the bag.
Both jobs are done.
The train can leave.
Now let’s follow the train into a bigger depot.
Three deliveries, nine robots.
The orchestrator runs the same graph query.
The model proposes the plan.

Relate shows which robot
can do each job, and when.

chapters: The same method with nine robots
